A1.justification: Both PDFs describe THREAD and retain the same central methodology and experiments. All 21 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v3, including appendices, tables, and figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Mind2Web and WikiHow experiments, an incident-mitigation study with on-call engineers, and ablations and backbone comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a multi-hop QA evaluation, GraphRAG comparisons, and preprocessing-cost results.

M1.justification: The five LU components, four LU types, extraction/merging process, prerequisite filtering, and linker-guided retrieval remain. FAQ and Appendix LU types move to Appendix A.4. Entity-relation linkers used for the new multi-hop evaluation were already described in v2. Appendix B.2.1 supplies implementation details for existing LU merging rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds 2WikiMultiHopQA inference and compositional questions, extending actual evaluation from procedural how-to tasks to factoid multi-hop reasoning. Mind2Web, WikiHow, and incident-mitigation coverage remains. The new scalability table uses those retained datasets rather than introducing additional coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds GraphRAG to the Mind2Web paradigm comparison in Table 6 and the incident case study in Appendix D.2. It removes the Synapse comparator, labeled SYNASE in v2 Table 2. MINDACT and the existing document, recursive, semantic, and proposition comparisons remain, making this a limited comparator-set revision.

E3.justification: The added multi-hop evaluation samples 200 inference/compositional questions and reports F1, EM, and accuracy; the cost analysis introduces per-document token and API-call accounting. Existing benchmark splits, model versions, and chunk/retrieval settings remain. IcM randomization wording changes from baseline ordering to assignment, but the PDFs do not establish that the study was redesigned or rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a comparative incident case study examining GraphRAG's incorrect retrieval and procedural responses. Appendix D.3 adds preprocessing-cost tradeoffs and an analysis across datasets of different sizes, substantially broadening failure and resource analysis. Existing history/selector ablations, document-format tests, and backbone comparisons remain; the backbone analysis is relocated to Appendix D.1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both specify temperature 0 and top_p 1; this retained decoding information does not constitute uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original THREAD scores remain, including Mind2Web element accuracy 68.29 and multi-turn WikiHow SR 72.16. v3 adds GraphRAG results in Table 6 (63.20 element accuracy, 65.09 operation F1, 56.90 step SR), multi-hop results favoring THREAD on all three plotted metrics in Figure 3, and cost results such as $0.045/document for THREAD versus $0.63 for Proposition in Table 11. The SYNASE result row is removed.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The conceptual LU definitions remain equivalent, and the WikiHow precision/recall formulas are retained after relocation to Appendix A.3. The added experiments introduce no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: v2 claims demonstrated effectiveness for how-to QA and explicitly leaves factoid evaluation unaddressed. v3's abstract and contribution list add demonstrated generalization to 5Ws and open-domain multi-hop questions, substantially extending the claimed applicability. The original logic-unit contribution and how-to performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of GraphRAG failures, preprocessing-cost tradeoffs, and scalability. Its limitations acknowledge the remaining breadth of untested open-domain tasks but remove the call to evaluate more backbones and retrievers. The rewritten selector discussion incorrectly attributes a performance drop to removing selection: unchanged Table 5 shows chunk element accuracy rising from 59.94 to 64.23 without selection.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2.1 newly identifies SpaCy header similarity for finding merge candidates and supplies the LU-merging prompt. Tables 11–12 disclose preprocessing tokens, API calls, and costs. Conversely, v3 omits v2's explicit two-simple/three-hard incident breakdown and manual mitigation-time estimate. Most existing prompts, hyperparameters, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ho et al. (2020) for 2WikiMultiHopQA and removes the Synapse and Xpert references. GraphRAG was already cited in v2; v3 develops a more explicit distinction between its entity relationships and THREAD's procedural logic. The broader related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: The paper undergoes extensive rewriting and reorganization: related work moves after analysis, experimental setup/results are regrouped, and document collection, metrics, two LU types, and backbone analysis move to appendices. Limitations move before references. Introductory and methodological explanations are revised substantially, although v3 introduces an unfinished prerequisite sentence in Section 2.1.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout and merges/redraws v2 Figures 2–3 into a combined construction-and-inference diagram. It adds the multi-hop Figure 3 and cost Tables 11–12, while relocating the retained backbone Figure 4. Tables receive revised sizing, coloring, and captions; Table 1 adds dataset-characteristic columns, and Table 3 replaces explicit difficulty labels with color coding.

improvement.justification: The tested GraphRAG comparator, previously missing multi-hop evaluation, explicit LU-merging instructions, and preprocessing-cost accounting modestly strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by reporting problems: Table 12 mislabels IcM/WikiHow success-rate gains as element accuracy, Section 4.1 contradicts the selector ablation, and the scalability argument compares different datasets without isolating scale. The original how-to evidence remains intact, supporting a limited net improvement.
